scope: dirty uncommitted snapshot with pre-artifact git diff HEAD --binary SHA-256 96af0c4611dd596aca70b291698f11d56d1f3923a9772194f0626b2c4a132045
canonical architecture, accepted decisions, runbooks, GitHub Plan and relevant open issues
public Investment Committee documentation, route and DTO contracts, implementation, migrations, configuration, source back-links, tests and CI
excludes PRD alignment because no PRD exists, live infrastructure observation, and independent branch-protection inspection
verdict: The implementation has sound core boundaries, but the 3,227-line concatenated architecture and adjacent public, operational, Plan, contract, and test claims contradict current behavior and are unsafe as an agent-development guide.

findings.impact: Module and workflow back-links point to a deleted document or ambiguous numeric sections in the concatenated architecture, so agents cannot reliably trace behavior to canonical intent.
findings.recommendation: Create stable named anchors in the concise architecture and update implicated module-level back-links in one mechanical pass; link detailed contracts to contract files or tests.

findings.impact: The declared cross-boundary dashboard DTOs disagree with shipped wire shapes and omit three endpoints, while type checking and check-contract do not compare those types to implementation.
findings.recommendation: Make contract/src/dashboards.d.ts own every shipped dashboard response and provenance union, consume those types in backend and tests, and add an executed DTO-conformance check.

findings.impact: Architecture is a concatenation of current state, copied specifications, plans, acceptance criteria and a second document, so headings are ambiguous and agents cannot distinguish durable guardrails from delivery history.
findings.recommendation: Replace it with a concise current-state guide covering guardrails, boundaries, components, trust and data flows, environments, an agent change map and links to canonical detail.

findings.impact: Docs promise a blocking golden-shape check, but preview and browser tests can replay a stale fixture and pass because no workflow executes a code-versus-golden shape assertion.
findings.recommendation: Implement the documented nonzero contract/field-shape CI gate or remove every blocking-gate claim and state that recapture is unaudited author responsibility.

findings.impact: A deployment can satisfy its docs while workers use the unrestricted DATABASE_URL, so the database permission boundary presented as an invariant is optional at runtime.
findings.recommendation: Decide whether rm_worker is mandatory outside ephemeral environments; either fail boot and document provisioning or describe it honestly as optional hardening.

findings.impact: The stated production environment inventory omits fail-closed credentials and names an obsolete RPC variable, so a by-the-book deployment can fail boot or leave required surfaces unusable.
findings.recommendation: Create one tested operator inventory for every production variable, consumer, default, secret status and fail-closed behavior; link architecture to it rather than duplicating values.

findings.impact: Canonical sections define incompatible persisted lifecycle state machines, so state changes and tests derived from one section cannot agree with the database or the other section.
findings.recommendation: Document only the six persisted states and describe brief publication as the scheduled-to-collecting transition or action.

findings.impact: A non-demo installation does not autonomously open or advance committee sessions, although architecture presents the queue cron chain as the operating model.
findings.recommendation: Until issue #208 lands, document committee scheduling as disabled and demo-driven; afterward document only the resolved environment contract and orchestration invariant.

findings.impact: Architecture overstates E2E execution for no-show publication, out-of-window rejection and cross-role denial, leaving named safety regressions able to remain green.
findings.recommendation: Add explicit assertions for the published no-show set, a post-close submission, member-to-analytics denial and member-to-admin denial, or narrow the claim.

findings.impact: Agents cannot tell whether a deterministic offline demo is supported or whether every demo and per-PR E2E is required to use live external providers.
findings.recommendation: State that demo and e2e defaults are live and ANALYTICS_SOURCE=hermetic is a local debugging or backend-test override, not a supported demo mode.

findings.impact: Architecture, shipped code, UI and contract disagree on lifecycle latency, queue observability, retry behavior and response envelopes.
findings.recommendation: Formally ratify synchronous 200/201 transitions or queued 202 actions in decisions and Plan, then delete the rejected specification.

findings.impact: Short non-actionable reasons pass validation and human audit text is propagated to worker-visible payload state contrary to the documented minimization boundary.
findings.recommendation: Enforce the shared 10-to-500 reason validator and carry only an audit request id in the job payload, or revise the canonical requirement with explicit rationale.

findings.impact: An agent implementing or calling the admin API from architecture will use nonexistent paths, methods, fields and queued response envelopes.
findings.recommendation: Delete endpoint and DTO catalogs from architecture; treat contract/src/routes.js and contract/src/admin.d.ts as canonical and retain only boundary and ownership summaries.

findings.impact: Worker and demo lifecycle calls can rewind existing sessions, report zero-row transitions as success, read future data, or perform an incomplete reopen that does not replace deadlines and jobs.
findings.recommendation: Resolve whether the listed domain corrections remain requirements; if so, implement them in the shared worker/admin domain path with adversarial state, timestamp and reopen tests, otherwise remove them from canonical docs and Plan.

findings.impact: Cloudflare and demo readiness can certify API or MCP while required dependencies are unavailable, defeating the documented shared health contract.
findings.recommendation: Define a shared health DTO, make readiness fail on required dependency loss, have MCP probe API, and execute negative dependency tests in CI.

findings.impact: The accepted production topology is not reproducible from repository-owned automation, and the no-proxy design contains no server that presents the documented Origin CA certificate.
findings.recommendation: Implement and test deployment and TLS or label D13 and D18 as target state and rewrite the runbook as a design checklist rather than an active GitOps procedure.

findings.impact: A prominently linked public guide directs prospective agent developers to nonexistent timing, files and scripts and describes host-generated content forbidden by the current protocol.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the page from the dynamic API and worker model or mark the static data explicitly historical, and add a route and behavior consistency test.

findings.impact: Superfield workers cannot resolve promised product authority and may follow deleted canonical documents or assume copied architecture plan text replaced them without an explicit decision.
findings.recommendation: Update Plan and issue canonical-doc metadata to surviving authorities; create a PRD if it has a distinct owner, otherwise stop requiring and referencing docs/prd.md.

clean_areas: Accepted decisions D1-D18 retain useful rationale and supersession history.
Frontend, backend and MCP cross the HTTP boundary through contract/src/routes.js, whose vendored runtime copy has a drift check.
Analytics token exclusivity, source-level updater isolation and rm_worker write denial have substantive tests.
Queue lanes and leases, forward-only migrations, roster snapshots, recommendation signatures and auth-before-SQL have executed coverage.
participation.html and api-reference.html agree on dynamic session discovery and signing routes and have route-literal consistency coverage.
Committed HEAD CI executed nonzero root, backend, MCP and Playwright test counts with loud Postgres provisioning and guarded live nightly suites.
unresolved_decisions: Are admin committee lifecycle actions intentionally synchronous 200/201 or required to be queued and return 202?
Is D13/D18 deployed current state, accepted target state, or external infrastructure whose automation lives elsewhere?
Is WORKER_DATABASE_URL mandatory outside ephemeral environments?
Does the repository need a separate PRD, or should the Plan stop requiring one?
Which goldens oracle is accepted: live-cluster shape comparison or offline contract conformance?
limitations: The review covers a dirty uncommitted snapshot identified by the recorded pre-artifact diff hash; the review artifacts themselves are outside that hash.
No PRD exists, so product-to-architecture traceability could not be established.
Full local backend tests were not rerun because Postgres was unavailable to the review worker; cited GitHub runs validate committed HEAD c42c47a, not dirty changes.
Branch-protection required contexts were not independently inspected.
Production and staging vendor infrastructure was not observed; deployment findings are limited to repository-owned evidence.
GitHub Plan and relevant issues were inspected, but merged issue and PR history was sampled rather than exhaustively replayed.
